Convex hull of points

Source: R/sp.R
cvhull.Rd

The smallest convex polygon holding every point, by Andrew's monotone chain with an exact orientation predicate (Shewchuk 1997), so near-collinear points never make a wrong turn. Points on an edge are not vertices; of coincident points the first is reported.

Usage

cvhull(x, y = NULL, lonlat = FALSE)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

lonlat

FALSE (the default) when x and y are planar coordinates in one length unit; TRUE when they are longitude and latitude in degrees, which are then projected to metres by eqproj() about their own centre, and centres are returned in degrees. It is never guessed.

Value

A list: idx, the row numbers of the vertices, anticlockwise from the point with the lowest x (then lowest y); area and perim, the hull's area and perimeter (in the square and the unit of the coordinates, or square metres and metres when lonlat = TRUE). One distinct point gives one vertex and zeros; collinear points give their two ends, area 0 and twice the segment's length. Each coordinate must be 0 or of magnitude from 1e-140 to 1e150, where the predicate is exact.

References

Andrew, A. M. (1979). Another efficient algorithm for convex hulls in two dimensions. Information Processing Letters, 9(5), 216-219. doi:10.1016/0020-0190(79)90072-3

Shewchuk, J. R. (1997). Adaptive precision floating-point arithmetic and fast robust geometric predicates. Discrete and Computational Geometry, 18(3), 305-363. doi:10.1007/PL00009321

Examples

cvhull(c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.5), c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.5))
#> $idx
#> [1] 1 2 3 4
#> 
#> $area
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $perim
#> [1] 4
#>
